name: CHINESE POKER
description: Chinese Poker, also known as Pusoy, Capsa Susun, or 13 Cards, is a card game where players arrange 13 cards into three poker hands (back, middle, front) that must increase in strength. Players compare corresponding hands against each opponent to win units.

content.text: Chinese Poker, also known as Pusoy, Capsa Susun, or 13 Cards, is a card game where players arrange 13 cards into three poker hands (back, middle, front) that must increase in strength. Players compare corresponding hands against each opponent to win units.

Country/Region of Origin: China/Hong Kong
Time Period: Traditional game, popularized in 20th century
Historical Development: Known as Sap Sam Cheung (十三張 - 13 cards) in Cantonese. Also called Luosong Pai Jiu (羅宋牌九 - Russian Pai Gow) in Chinese. Distantly related to Pai Gow.
Cultural Significance: Popular gambling game in Hong Kong, Southeast Asia, and among Asian communities in the USA.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: No, each plays for themselves

Type: Standard 52-card pack
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: None
No wild cards

Standard 52-card pack
Agreed stake per unit
Table space for arranging hands

Cards per Player: 13 cards each
Dealing Pattern: Singly, clockwise
All cards dealt at once
